page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.d1.6xlarge is an x86_64 architecture server instance powered by an Intel Xeon E5-2682v4 processor running at 2.5 GHz. It features 24 dedicated physical cores with 24 vCPUs, utilizing a single thread per core configuration. The instance is equipped with 96.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced allocation of 4.0 GB of RAM per core.

A defining characteristic of this instance is its massive local storage capacity, offering 70,866 GB of local HDD storage. This makes the server highly suitable for storage-intensive workloads. Network connectivity is supported by an 8 Gbps baseline bandwidth, running on a KVM hypervisor. No dedicated GPU hardware is included in this configuration.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the ecs.d1.6xlarge provides a high density of local HDD storage relative to its compute and memory resources, making it a cost-effective choice for large-scale data archiving, distributed file systems, and cold storage applications. The dedicated CPU allocation ensures consistent processing performance, though the reliance on HDD storage rather than NVMe SSDs represents a tradeoff, prioritizing capacity over high-IOPS random read/write speeds. Appropriate workloads include MapReduce jobs, big data processing, and large-scale log storage.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.d1.6xlarge is a storage-focused server instance designed for capacity-intensive workloads. Powered by an Intel Xeon E5-2682v4 processor, it features 24 dedicated physical cores and 24 vCPUs running at 2.5 GHz on an x86_64 architecture. The hardware configuration includes 96.0 GB of system memory and an exceptionally large local storage capacity of 70,866 GB utilizing HDD technology. Operating on a KVM hypervisor, the instance delivers an 8 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. With no integrated GPU, this server is optimized for data density and sequential storage operations rather than acceleration. The high ratio of HDD storage to compute resources makes it qualitatively cost-efficient for massive data archiving, distributed file systems, and big data processing pipelines where storage volume is prioritized over high-IOPS solid-state performance.
